item.title: PM opens Bangladesh Innovation Fair 2026
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman today inaugurated a three-day "Bangladesh Innovation Fair 2026".
He laid importance on turning home-grown innovations into commercial products and connecting them directly with the market.
The fair, organized by Ministry of Science and Technology is being held at Novo Theatre at Bijoy Sarani with the theme "Innovate to Market".
The fair aims to build sustainable partnerships among local innovators and innovative organisations, policymakers, entrepreneurs, investors, educational institutions, financial institutions and development partners.
Government and private research organisations, 73 public and private universities, independent researchers, students, emerging startups, small and medium enterprises (SMEs) and global investors are participating in the fair.
More than 1,000 new and promising innovations in technology, business, education, health, agriculture, environment and other sectors are being showcased at the event.
The organisers said many promising technologies and ideas are developed at the grassroots level but failed to reach implementation stage due to a lack of policy support, initial funding and institutional cooperation.
Removing such administrative and financial barriers and ensuring intellectual property protection and commercial expansion is the major objective of the fair, they said.
On the second day of the fair tomorrow, a special international session titled ‘Healthcare Innovation for All: Expanding Access to Affordable and Inclusive Healthcare’ will be held.
The session will discuss technologies for delivering affordable, quality healthcare to marginalised people at their doorsteps.
Prime Minister’s wife Dr Zubaida Rahman will attend the tomorrow’s session as the chief guest.
National Board of Revenue (NBR), Department of Patents, Industrial Designs and Trademarks (DPDT) and Foreign Investors’ Chamber of Commerce and Industry (FICCI) are strategic partners of the fair, while the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) is providing technical support.

item.title: Rizvi stresses education, self-reliance to empower women
item.description:
BNP Acting Secretary General Ruhul Kabir Rizvi on Saturday expressed hope that violence against women including rape, child abuse and all forms of wrongdoing would be eliminated from society.
“We will wipe out rape, violence against women, child abuse and all kinds of wrongdoing from this society,” he said.
He made the remarks before a rally organised in the capital’s Nayapaltan marking the 48th founding anniversary of Jatiyatabadi Mahila Dal.
He said the government led by BNP Chairman and Prime Minister Tarique Rahman would ensure women’s civic dignity, right to live and legal rights.
“For this, there are two things. Women must be enlightened through education, and women must become mentally self-reliant. The government has taken many efforts and initiatives to make women mentally self-reliant,” Rizvi said.
He also highlighted education as another key means of empowering women.
Rizvi said the leaders of Jatiyatabadi Mohila Dal are not incompetent and are equally capable of running the state.
“Those who are its leaders, whether at the district level, metropolitan level or central level, none of them is incompetent. They are highly qualified. They are equally capable of running a state and an institution,” he said.
He said BNP’s assumption of power meant that every party worker is now part of the government, not merely those holding official positions.
He said people could now speak and move around freely, while women could travel without fear, and recalled the persecution faced by Mahila Dal leaders during the previous government.
He urged Mahila Dal leaders and activists to closely follow the government’s programmes, particularly its contributions to people and social protection, and communicate those initiatives to the public.
He urged Mahila Dal members to inform people about the government’s measures, particularly those concerning women, saying they are part of both the party and the government.
He said the prime minister’s mother, Begum Khaleda Zia, had made education free up to the intermediate level, with no tuition fees required for girls studying at schools and colleges.
“And her eldest son has said that education up to the degree and honours levels will be free, with no tuition fees for girls’ education,” Rizvi said.
He described the initiatives as public welfare measures aimed at empowering women through education and making them financially self-reliant.
“These programs and initiatives of Tarique Rahman have to be explained to people, communicated to them and spread among them. That is your responsibility because you are part of this party and part of the government,” he said.
Rizvi then inaugurated the colourful rally marking the 48th founding anniversary of Jatiyatabadi Mahila Dal.

item.title: PM urges youth to step forward in nation-building
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has called on the country’s youth to take responsibility for rebuilding the nation, saying no one can stop them if they unite with that goal.
Referring to the events of August 5, 2024, he said the youth had already demonstrated their ability to bring about change by ousting the “fascist regime”.
“We must build this nation. Therefore, the responsibility of rebuilding the state rests with the youth. Everyone must unite to build a clean and tidy country,” he said.
The prime minister made the remarks on Saturday morning while addressing the inauguration of a nationwide three-month dengue prevention and control campaign at the South Plaza of the National Parliament House.
“I seek your assistance. To the best of my knowledge, there are approximately 2.3 million Scouts and 22,000 BNCC members in Bangladesh,” he said.
“Furthermore, excluding primary schools and madrasas, the number of students in high schools, madrasas, colleges and universities across the country is around 15 million. Including primary schools and madrasas, the total reaches 25 million.”
He said the large youth population could play a significant role in transforming the country.
“If such a vast youth population wants to transform the country, it is entirely possible. The youth demonstrated to the entire world on August 5, 2024, that they are capable of bringing about change,” Tarique said.
“The youth initiated that change. So, let us unite here today with the resolve to tackle the dengue problem over the next three months. We may not achieve 100% success, but we can certainly achieve at least 80%.”
The prime minister said the responsibility of rebuilding the country now rests with the youth.
“With so many of us, if we truly wish to rebuild the nation, can anyone stop us? No one can. Now, the responsibility of building the country rests with you,” he said.
He also called for a nationwide cleanliness drive.
“We have gathered here today—thousands of us in this field, and millions more across every district of the country—united by a single goal: to clean our nation and strive to make it free of waste,” he said.
Local Government Minister Dr Abdul Moyeen Khan, State Minister Mir Shahe Alam, Dhaka South City Administrator Abdus Salam and Dhaka North City Administrator Shafiqul Alam Khan Milton also spoke at the event.
After inaugurating the campaign, the prime minister visited various stalls dedicated to dengue awareness.

item.title: Rain, thundershowers likely over 8 divisions
item.description:
Bangladesh Meteorological Department (BMD) has forecast rain or thundershowers in all divisions of the country, including Dhaka, in 24 hours commencing 9am on Saturday.
“Light to moderate rain or thundershowers accompanied by temporary gusty winds is likely to occur at many places over Rangpur, Mymensingh, Khulna and Sylhet divisions and at a few places over Rajshahi, Dhaka, Barisal and Chittagong divisions with moderately heavy to heavy falls at places over the country,” Met Office said.
Day and night temperatures may fall slightly over the country.
The low over coastal areas of Odisha-Andhra Pradesh now lies over South Chhattisgarh and adjoining areas.
The axis of monsoon troughs runs through Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh, the centre of the low, Bihar, Gangetic West Bengal to Assam across southern part of Bangladesh.
Monsoon is fairly active over Bangladesh and moderate over North Bay.

item.title: Chhatra Dal leader missing after falling into Padma River
item.description:
A local leader of Jatiyatabadi Chhatra Dal (JCD) went missing after falling into the Padma River when a boat carrying 123 people hit a pillar of the Hardinge Bridge in Bheramara upazila of Kushtia district on Friday night.
The Chhatra Dal leader was identified as Rakibuzzaman Rocky, member secretary of the Shailkupa municipality unit JCD in Jhenaidah.
Mohammad Zahedur Rahman, Officer-in-Charge of Bheramara Police Station, said a group of people hired a boat to visit the Solaiman Shah Shrine in Bheramara from Katla Ghat in Shailkupa of Jhenaidah district.
When the boat was returning after visiting the shrine, it was hit by a strong current, causing it to collide with a pillar of the bridge.
At one point, three people, including Rocky, fell into the river as the rear portion of the bulkhead boat collided with pillar No. 4 of the Hardinge Bridge.
Two of the victims, Liton and Wahab, were rescued, but Rocky remained missing.
Divers from the local fire service conducted a rescue operation but failed to trace Rocky until 1am on Saturday.
Bheramara Upazila Nirbahi Officer Mohammad Amirul Arafat, who visited the scene, said darkness and the strong river current were making the rescue operation difficult, while several government units were working at the scene.
Assistant Director of Kushtia Fire Service and Civil Defence Wadud Hossain said: “Due to the strong current in the Padma, it has become difficult to conduct the search operation at night.”

item.title: Is the iPhone 18 Pro a true generational leap?
item.description:
Last Thursday, as I was watching the Apple September event, the exact moment Tim Cook stepped aside and moved John Ternus toward center stage —"no no no, not me, that's your guy, that's your opener”—felt less like a casual baton pass and more like a gravitational pivot the industry had been waiting for.
The engineer who built Apple's silicon transition from the inside became its CEO at the exact moment Apple shipped its most coherent product generation in a decade: the M6 Mac Mini, the M5 MacBooks, M5 Max, M5 Ultra, and the A20 Pro iPhone.
Same commitment, across every device Apple makes, simultaneously. This is more than a product refresh cycle.
Apple does not believe the future of AI lives in a data centre.
It believes the future of AI lives in your hand, on your lap or your desk — running locally, privately, without a server, without your data leaving your device.
Apple spent the past four years building the best inference machine that you and I, the general population, can actually buy.
Ternus made that philosophy explicit from his very first keynote: the iPhone is no longer just a smartphone; it is an intelligent personal hub you start your day with.
The iPhone 18 Pro is the first product built explicitly around that philosophy. Everything Apple did inside this device is the engineering consequence of that single bet.
Welcome to Ramgageddon
At a glance, the 18 Pro and Pro Max look very similar to last year’s 17 Pros.
You still get the aluminium unibody with Ceramic Shield 2 on the front and Ceramic Shield on the back, but they are now all color-matched instead of two-tone.
This year you can enjoy the new flagship Burgundy color, alongside Glacier, Silver, and finally, matte Black.
However, the first major upgrade for the Pros is the price. Given the hyper memory inflation we have seen across the entire Apple product line—driven by the massive RAM inflation for AI—both models are now up by $100.
The 18 Pro starts at $1,199 and the Pro Max at $1,299, with a new 2TB storage option.
That stings less than what Apple quietly did to the models it did not update. The iPhone Air moves to $1,099, base 17 to $899, and the 17e to $699. There was no iPhone 18.
Today, we are here for the Pros.
A20 Pro: The desktop class architecture
After three years of 3nm chips, the A20 Pro is Apple's first smartphone chip built on cutting-edge 2-nanometer technology.
The CPU holds the same 6-core arrangement as the A19 Pro: two super cores running 20% faster than their predecessors, and four efficiency cores, all integrated with neural accelerators for low-latency, on-device AI.
But the GPU moves to a 7-core design, accommodating up to 40% performance increase driven by expanded internal bandwidth and a new generation of neural accelerators with 2x faster 8-bit floating-point math.
But neither the CPU nor the GPU is where the real change happened.
The Neural Engine is. Apple doubled it. The A20 Pro features a dual 16-core Neural Engine just like the newly introduced M6 Mac Mini, delivering twice the AI compute of the A19 Pro.
For context, the 32 Neural Engine cores were previously reserved for the Mac Ultra.
Apple has pulled that architecture into a phone.
Feeding all of it results in a 50% increase in memory bandwidth— the widest memory interface Apple has ever shipped in an iPhone.
Raw core counts are just ideas without the bandwidth to keep them going when you need them.
Packing this much compute into a smartphone chassis created a thermal constraint that a conventional vapor chamber could not resolve.
Apple resolved it at the silicon packaging level.
The A20 Pro introduces custom chip packaging directly inspired by the M-series packaging, with the silicon die now sitting side-by-side with memory rather than stacked beneath it.
This single repositioning removes the memory from the thermal path of the SoC.
The chip sits flush against the vapor chamber. What previously acted as insulation is now out of the way entirely.
The vapor chamber itself was rebuilt from scratch. It carries three times the surface area compared to the 17 Pro's, cycling deionized water continuously across a structure made from 80% recycled stainless steel.
A larger graphite plate handles the remaining thermal load. The critical addition is nanotwin copper, an industry-first material that moves heat specifically away from the display while maintaining structural strength.
The combined result is a 40% improvement in not just peak benchmark numbers, but sustained performance over the 17 Pro, and a 2x improvement over the 16 Pro.
The logic board was also redesigned entirely to fit a larger battery.
The result is visible in the most honest metric available: weight.
The iPhone 18 Pros are the heaviest Pro Apple has ever shipped.
Variable aperture: Hardware, finally
The camera is arguably the most important part of the iPhone experience, and with the iPhone 18 Pro, Apple introduced its biggest upgrade in years: a true Variable Aperture.
Aperture controls how much light enters the sensor and dictates depth of field.
On every previous iPhone, you had only two ways of controlling the light: ISO and shutter speed.
A fixed aperture, like the f/1.78, was the constraint you worked around. Cranking ISO to handle low light caused graininess because you were amplifying sensor sensitivity without controlling the incoming light itself. The physics were always working against you.
The new 48MP Fusion main camera removes that constraint.
Apple has created a system of six laser-cut polymer blades, each thinner than a human hair, all controlled by a custom rotor mechanism. This rotor can mechanically adjust the aperture between four specific positions: f/1.48, f/1.8, f/2.8, and f/4.0.
If you open it up to f/1.48 or f/1.8, you are letting in 50% more light, which is perfect for low-light and astrophotography.
But if you stop it down to f/4.0, you can really make sure the entire scene is in focus.
For the average person, this means no more blurry faces in the back row of group dinner shots, and no more grainy, unusable night photos.
This is the first time you actually have control over depth of field at a hardware level.
The frictionless ecosystem
The N1 networking chip is a transition management story. Real-world throughput lives in the seams—the exact moment your phone shifts from Wi-Fi 7 to cellular or routes a call across two simultaneous connections without dropping a word.
The N1 is engineered specifically to make those handoffs completely invisible.
Pair that with Apple’s in-house C2 modem packaged alongside the A20 Pro—guaranteeing a noticeable bump to internet speeds and reliability even when you are stuck in traditional dead zones, and the hardware finally catches up to how we actually live and work on the move.
Additionally, iPhone Handoff routes a single phone number transparently across two iPhones to whichever iPhone you pick up via invisible, modem-level carrier negotiation.
If you carry a work phone and a personal phone, this feature alone will fundamentally change how you navigate your day.
Apple also managed to fit part of Face ID under the display, allowing the Dynamic Island to shrink 35% compared to the 17 Pro. It is now far more useful, capable of displaying three live activities at a glance. A small change that compounds in usefulness when the device is routing this much information at once.
Another key improvement is the battery life. The iPhone 18 Pro carries a 4,056 mAh cell, delivering 36 hours of video playback compared to 33 hours on the 17 Pro.
The Pro Max is the more dramatic story — 5,391 mAh, 45 hours of video playback.
That is at least 6 hours more than the 17 Pro Max, driven by a significantly larger battery cell alongside the chip’s efficiency improvements.
On eSIM-only models, the numbers are even bigger: 4,288 and 5,567 mAh. If endurance is your primary concern, the Max has never made a stronger case for itself.
The charging architecture now matches the power draw: 50% charge in 15 minutes, roughly 20% faster than the previous generation.
Just five minutes of wired charging delivers approximately 6 hours of video playback.
For a device running sustained workloads across a full day, that is more than a convenience feature.
The intelligence layer
The 32-core Neural Engine is not a Siri feature. Siri is a Neural Engine feature. The chip came first.
Every improvement in Siri AI — on-device personal context across apps, real-time action inside 300,000 third-party applications, expressive voices — exists only because Apple built the hardware to run it locally, without a server, without latency, without your data leaving the device. That is the architecture. Siri is what sits on top of it.
One precision matters here. Apple's on-device models are excellent at what they do. Frontier AI capabilities — GPT-4 class reasoning, complex multi-step analysis — still run in data centres regardless of what device you hold.
The 32-core Neural Engine does not change that ceiling.
What it changes is the floor: the baseline of what this device can do privately, instantly, and without a network connection. That is the bet Apple is making.
Together with state-of-the-art hardware, a handful of incredibly handy software-level improvements have arrived.
Pro controls make the manual capabilities accessible without requiring a third-party app: aperture selection between four positions, shutter speed, white balance, and a histogram for exposure monitoring, all built into the native camera interface.
Photographic Styles received an upgrade. Apple added texture and grain control, allowing you to fine-tune the interplay between light and shadow or adjust skin texture to elevate the emotion of a scene.
You can balance color and texture simultaneously, and crucially, reverse or change these edits at any time.
The 18 Pro brings a much-needed double-tap tracking feature that keeps your focus on any subject, no matter where they move around in the frame.
Plus, it comes with stunning 4K Dolby Vision HDR time-lapses and Cinematic mode effects that you can add to your regular videos after you have captured them—now with 60 frames per second for smooth half-speed playback.
This transforms the device into an uncompromising mobile camera rig.
AudioMix receives a meaningful update too: music now joins voice as a supported input type.
For field production, this eliminates the binary choice between capturing your subject’s voice or the acoustic environment surrounding them.
Combined with ProRes Log recording and Smart Focus Tracking, the 18 Pro now becomes a true camera-to-edit solution for run-and-gun production.
This is exactly why Samsung has not quite won over the “Shot on iPhone” crowd.
Finally, “Image Authenticity” is where Apple makes its most consequential long-term statement.
Apple goes beyond fallible watermarks. Supporting the SynthID standard to identify AI-generated images is the industry baseline, but Apple is going a step further with the “Apple Reference Image.”
Now you can mathematically prove the authenticity of a photo taken on an iPhone 18 Pro.
Apple Reference Image starts in the most secure way possible: with the sensor.
The new main sensor securely and digitally signs photo metadata at the pixel level the exact moment of capture.
Private Cloud Compute develops that signed data into an unalterable image in the Photos a pp that acts as a digital negative to visually confirm what was actually in the shot.
This reference photo lives alongside the regular editable photo for flexibility, setting a standard that should become a universal standard for every camera on Earth.
Verdict
What does it signal about the industry?
The spec war — thinner, lighter, brighter, marginally better camera benchmarks — is structurally over. Apple has now replaced it with a different competition entirely: sustained compute density.
For the past two years, the tech industry settled into a comfortable consensus: Apple was losing the AI race.
OpenAI rewrote what an assistant could do. Google embedded Gemini across its entire product suite. Meta open-sourced its models and dared everyone to keep up.
Apple, meanwhile, partnered with OpenAI and now Google. The industry read that as surrender.
They are wrong.
The writer is a contributor and tech enthusiast

item.title: Zero IRF: Who will bear the costs of free service?
item.description:
Fire, water, open space, and air are mankind's original commons.
While air remains the most free-flowing of them all, it still requires money under certain conditions, and the breath in our lungs carries a cost in today's post-industrial era.
Let us draw a parallel to the Bangladesh Bank's recent decision to slash down to zero the interchange reimbursement fee or IRF, which is the vital earning source of the participating institutions that provide mobile financial services (MFS).
Not just this monetary transaction facility, but also any utilities free of costs -- be it telecommunications and banking services or use of electricity -- could have been considered the most loved thing to modern people, had there been no charges!
The central bank has made the policy shift by cutting IRF to be zero and MDR can be set at zero with the lifting of 1% floor price effective from October 1, 2026.
This directive for 'Bangla QR' system has been issued to further popularize digital payments.
It allows customers to make direct payments simply by scanning a merchant's QR (Quick Response) code using their bank or MFS apps, a revolutionary step towards attaining transparency in daily commerce and a cashless society.
In Bangladesh, we expect that the government provides energy subsidy without actually targeting the vulnerable groups who need and deserve it.
As a result, such policy turns unsustainable, and the people have to pay multiple prices to get access to energy. Also, the farmers have been incurring losses over the years as a consequence of a populist policy of, say, for example, keeping rice price low.
Now, the question arises: would a zero IRF and MDR not expose the entire digital payment ecosystem to severe structural risks as the measure removes an 'organic revenue model that funds network infrastructure, security upgrades and fraud prevention'?
None can deny that zero fees are consumer-friendly, only on paper, however. Industry innovators apprehend that this decision would jeopardize the institutions that have invested in building the digital payment infrastructure.
Many others may either ignore or be unaware of the fact that behind every seamless QR transaction lies a complex web of expenses: technology maintenance, agent incentives, distribution networks, mobile network operator charges, customer service, and settlement costs.
This means removing the IRF and MDR strips the platforms of their capacity to recover these essential operating costs.
Similar digital payment was 'free' in India where the government has borne the costs by giving subsidies, but that subsidy, too, is going to be withdrawn anytime.
Given the current fiscal constraints, it is not advisable either that the government of Bangladesh subsidize the costs of going cashless.
At the same time, making zero IRF and MDR to pave the way for popularizing Bangla QR is tantamount to punishing MFS operators who have made investments and driven the vast majority of digital financial transactions.
The process of converting hard cash into digital balance (cash-in) and vice versa (cash-out) relies on a massive network of human agents and distributors, according to the business model.
Managing this expansive infrastructure is financed through a delicate balance of transaction fees, service commissions, and merchant discount rates or MDR.
The government would lose revenues in the form of value-added tax (VAT) for every transaction under this model.
The MFS provider's subsidy for a single Tk1,000 cash-in transaction could stand at Tk6.40.
This begs another question: If the financial spine of the existing digital infrastructure is weakened in the name of incentivizing cashless transactions, who will foot the bill in the long run?
Cuts in fees for agents under the circumstances may work as a disincentive for this army of people, numbering around 2.4 million to remain engaged in MFS.
This human network has democratized financial services, reaching the under-banked and unbanked masses even in remote places.
If the agent-driven ecosystem is dismantled to force a new digital payment model prematurely, years of hard-earned progress in financial inclusion may be reversed.
In zero IRF and MDR regime, some desperate merchants and/or agents may find incentive to make fake payments and still take certain commissions bypassing the system. Transactions of ill-gotten money or money laundering through fake payments cannot be ruled out.
Already allegations have it that some agents and merchants are exploiting Bangla QR codes to facilitate informal cash-out services for customers without any actual exchange of goods or services.
On paper, these look like progressive digital payments, but in reality, they are merely disguised cash withdrawals.
Such practice would artificially inflate official digital transaction data; it distorts the true picture of digital commerce in the country. Industry experts warn that a zero-IRF and MDR policy will likely amplify this malpractice.
An unintended consequence of this policy is likely to be the squeezing of MFS providers, who may eventually be forced to impose new charges on basic cash-in services.
This would create a lose-lose scenario: the government's revenues contract, while the transaction costs for ordinary citizens rise.
Since Bangla QR is deeply intertwined with the broader digital payment grid, a one-sided measure of introducing zero fees may be counterproductive.
Thus, the central bank may think of devising a balanced tariff structure through discussions with the stakeholders.
If QR codes become a tool to bypass standard cash-out channels without driving real retail commerce, it is feared that Bangla QR will end up deviating from its core objective of fostering a genuine cashless economy.
Salahuddin Bablu is a journalist

item.title: FIFA rebuffs Morocco claim over 2030 World Cup final
item.description:
FIFA said on Friday that a decision on the venue for the 2030 World Cup final would be made "in due course", after Moroccan football federation president Fouzi Lekjaa said the showpiece match would be staged in Morocco.
Morocco, Spain and Portugal are co-hosting the 2030 tournament and have already begun competing for the right to stage the final, with Madrid's Santiago Bernabeu and a planned 115,000-seat stadium in Benslimane, near Casablanca, viewed as the leading contenders.
Lekjaa said on Wednesday that the final would take place in Morocco.
"Benslimane province will host the World Cup final. Whether some people like it or not," Lekjaa said during a public meeting in the region, according to video published by local media.
However, FIFA said no decision had yet been taken.
"As communicated on 5 August 2026, a decision will be made by FIFA in due course," a FIFA spokesperson told AFP on Friday.
The comments prompted reaction in Spain, where Real Madrid coach Jose Mourinho backed the Santiago Bernabeu as the ideal venue for the final.
"I would like the final to be in Lisbon, but I'm already happy that a country like ours will have at least one match (at the World Cup)," the Portuguese coach told reporters on Friday.
"If you can play in a legendary, historic stadium, where some of the greatest players in history have played, the stadium of the most important club in the history of football, then I think it should be here," Mourinho said, referring to the Bernabeu.
"If I were Benfica's coach, I would tell you exactly the same thing."

item.title: Razaullah’s fearless Edgbaston assault gives Pakistan a lift
item.description:
Pakistan pacer Razaullah produced a stunning counterattacking display on Test debut to give Pakistan a much-needed boost in their World Test Championship clash against England at Edgbaston.
The 21-year-old walked in at 9 with the score at 312/7 and Pakistan still needing another 8 runs to make England bat again, and went on an assault, smashing 81 from just 63 deliveries.
His nine sixes equalled the record for most sixes by a debutant in a Test innings and helped Pakistan set England a fourth-innings target of 130 after being pushed to the brink.
Razaullah’s approach was one of fearless aggression, particularly against the short ball, as he took on Jofra Archer, Gus Atkinson and Josh Tongue.
“I was being selective with which balls to slog, but they all seemed within range,” he said after the conclusion of Day 3.
“I wanted to take it as deep as possible. I wasn’t scared of pace.
“I wanted to punish the balls from Archer that landed on a hard length.
“There’s nothing to be scared of when you’re playing for your country.
“I was just enjoying myself.”
At Edgbaston, he backed himself against an England attack that had repeatedly troubled Pakistan’s batters during the series, which gave the home side an unassailable 2-0 lead from the opening two Tests.
“My favourite ball [to face] is the short ball. I just believed in myself.
“I thought if I played 50 balls, I’d get a positive result. And thankfully that happened.”
Razaullah’s intent was matched by the enjoyment he displayed at the crease, soaking in the reception as the Edgbaston crowd stood up to commemorate his fighting spirit.
“I enjoyed the standing ovation.
“I like to enjoy life and I was relishing the moment.”
England will begin Day 4 with the bat, needing 130 runs to make it 3-0 in the three-match series.

item.title: Zverev holds off Khachanov, Shelton powers past Tiafoe to reach US Open final
item.description:
Top seed Alexander Zverev out-gunned Karen Khachanov to reach his third straight Grand Slam final on Friday, rolling into the US Open title match with a straight sets win.
Big-serving Ben Shelton overpowered American compatriot Frances Tiafoe in four sets to reach the first Grand Slam final of his career.
Zverev, who followed up his maiden major at the French Open with a runner-up finish at Wimbledon, saved two set points in the final tiebreaker to close out the 6-3, 7-6 (9/7), 7-6 (8/6) victory.
He'll face Ben Shelton in Sunday's championship match.
The German predicted an "absolutely epic" contest between the two Americans, after which he'll be out to thwart the winner's bid to become the first American man in 23 years to lift a Grand Slam trophy.
"Hopefully I can not make the American dream come true on Sunday," said Zverev, who came agonizingly close to the US Open title in 2020 before falling to Dominic Thiem in five sets.
After a somewhat inauspicious start to the tournament, spending nine hours and 26 minutes on court in laborious five-set victories in the first and second rounds, Zverev has steadily upped his game.
He needed two hours and 57 minutes to deny 50th-ranked Khachanov's bid to become the lowest-ranked Grand Slam finalist since number 54 Marcos Baghdatis at the 2006 Australian Open.
But the Russian, who fell to Zverev in the Olympic gold medal match in Tokyo in 2021, put up a spirited challenge in the second and third sets.
Unable to make any real headway in the first set, Khachanov fell a quick break down in the second.
The Russian couldn't resist a grin when he snuck a passing shot by Zverev to open the fourth game, and flung his arm into the air in celebration three points later when a forehand winner gave him his first break chance of the match.
Zverev double faulted to hand him a break that leveled the set at 2-2.
Khachanov had another chance two games later when Zverev's backhand into the net to end a 32-shot rally gave him a break point.
But the German came up with a big serve and escaped the danger as they went to the tiebreaker, where Khachanov denied Zverev on two set points with thumping forehand and a brilliant backhand down the line before Zverev closed out the set.
Neither player mustered a break point in a tense third set. Khachanov had a chance to extend the match when he took a 6-4 lead in the tiebreaker, but after a pair of forehand errors from the Russian Zverev came up with his 15th ace and sealed the win on the next point when Khachanov sent a forehand long.
Eighth-seeded Shelton blasted 20 aces on his way to a thrilling 4-6, 6-3, 6-3, 7-5 victory on the Arthur Ashe Stadium court that sends the 23-year-old into Sunday's championship match against top-seeded Alexander Zverev of Germany.
A pulsating all-American semi-final had seen both players vying to reach a Grand Slam final for the first time.
Shelton -- who took down defending champion Carlos Alcaraz in the quarter-finals -- will now have the chance to become the first American man to win a Grand Slam title since 2003, when Andy Roddick triumphed at the US Open.
"It's a lot of emotion," Shelton said in an on-court interview after a win that was watched by a star-studded New York crowd.
"My dad, my mom have sacrificed a lot for me to be in this position today. My dad lost his mom earlier this year, and she's the reason that he was able to play tennis.
"Without her, there's no Ben Shelton standing here today. So this one is for her. And I'm gonna need you guys on Sunday to to bring the energy. I'm going for it. I'm gonna leave it all on the court.
Earlier, Tiafoe got off to a bright start, claiming the first set after breaking when Shelton uncharacteristically double-faulted to trail at 5-4.
Tiafoe held to love to clinch the first set but Shelton came flying out of the blocks to start the second.
An early break helped him into a 2-0 lead before Tiafoe responded with a break to level at 2-2.
Yet with Tiafoe's serve increasingly erratic, Shelton grabbed another break in the eighth game to go 5-3 up and then held to level.
The momentum was all with Shelton and Tiafoe had to fight off two break points before holding early in the third set.
However Shelton – who had one serve initially clocked at 158mph before it was later adjusted to 144mph -- made no mistake in the fifth game with a break to go 3-2 up.
Tiafoe needed to hold to keep the set alive in the ninth game, and a furious arm-wrestle saw the 11th seed once again save three break and set points.
Shelton though earned his fourth break point after pouncing on Tiafoe's second serve once more, scorching a backhand return down the line.
Shelton converted that when Tiafoe netted a forehand to find himself 2-1 down.
The fourth set went with serve until the 12th game, when Shelton grabbed the crucial break to seal victory.

item.title: World changing with BRICS: What Bangladesh should do
item.description:
INDIA-BRICS-SUMMIT

The map of power in world politics is never static. States that were once on the periphery of international decision-making may move towards the centre as they gain economic power.

The rise of BRICS should be understood within this larger historical change. It is not just a collaborative framework of emerging economies, but rather a political question concerning the uneven distribution of power, wealth, representation, and decision-making in the current international system.

The name 'BRICS' originates from the initials of Brazil, Russia, India, China, and South Africa. Over time, its scope has expanded significantly.

Currently, BRICS has 11 member countries: Brazil, Russia, India, China, South Africa, Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, United Arab Emirates, Saudi Arabia, and Indonesia. Additionally, several countries have been granted partnership status.

Hence, BRICS is no longer a limited platform of five countries; it is becoming an important manifestation of the economic and political aspirations of the wider global South.

Why is BRICS important?

Post-World War II international economic and political institutions were established at a time when many of today's emerging powers had comparatively limited economic and diplomatic capacity.

However, the centre of gravity of the world economy has gradually shifted. China and India have become major economic powers; Brazil, Indonesia, South Africa, Saudi Arabia, and the United Arab Emirates play significant roles in their respective regions and the global economy.

This raises the question—if the real power distribution of the world economy changes, why should the framework for international decision-making remain unchanged? BRICS has essentially entered this area of imbalance.

One of its main goals is to make the international system more multipolar, representative, and sensitive to the developing world.

Strengthening the voice of developing countries in international monetary and developmental frameworks, increasing financing for infrastructure and sustainable development, expanding trade and investment among members, increasing opportunities for transactions in local currencies, and strengthening mutual cooperation in international crises—these are all part of BRICS' broader objectives.

Iran's Pezeshkian meets Modi in New Delhi

A significant institutional achievement of BRICS is the New Development Bank. This bank finances projects in infrastructure, energy, water, urbanisation, transportation, environment, and sustainable development.
Its aim is not to dissolve traditional international financial institutions but to create an additional pathway for financing for developing countries.

Is BRICS a threat to other regional organisations? It is important to clarify that BRICS is not, in essence, a regional organisation.

Its members do not belong to any specific geographical region. It includes countries from Asia, Africa, the Middle East, and Latin America.

Therefore, there is no direct competition with regional organisations like the South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation, the Association of Southeast Asian Nations, or African regional institutions.

Instead, the rise of BRICS raises the most questions about the dominance of those international frameworks where Western influence has historically been strong.

However, viewing BRICS as an 'anti-Western coalition' would be an oversimplification.

India, for example, is an important member of BRICS while also having deep strategic ties with the United States, Japan, and Australia.

The United Arab Emirates and Saudi Arabia also maintain close economic and security relationships with the Western world.

Hence, the real significance of BRICS is probably not in replacing the West but in creating an alternative arena for negotiation in the international system.

What can Bangladesh achieve?

For Bangladesh, the significance of BRICS is multifaceted. Firstly, Bangladesh requires substantial infrastructure financing for its next stage of development.

Bangladesh has been a member of the New Development Bank since 2021. By the end of 2025, the amount of approved financing from the bank for Bangladesh has reached approximately 450 million USD.

In other words, Bangladesh's relationship with BRICS is not just at a level of political interest; a functional financial foundation has already been established.

Secondly, BRICS can expand Bangladesh's sphere of economic diplomacy. China and India are two very important economic partners for Bangladesh.

At the same time, the BRICS member states in the Middle East are important for Bangladesh's energy security, labour market, and investment. There is also the opportunity to expand commercial relations with countries like Brazil, South Africa, and Indonesia.

BRICS nations slam Trump tariffs, condemn strikes on Iran

Thirdly, after graduating from the list of least developed countries, Bangladesh will need to find new sources of foreign financing, market access, and development partnerships.

BRICS can be an additional diplomatic and economic support in that period of change.

Fourthly, engagement with BRICS can give further effective multiplicity to Bangladesh's foreign policy based on 'friendship with all'.

The strategic success of a small or medium power state does not always lie in confining itself to one power centre; instead, it lies in maintaining relationships with multiple power centres and expanding its negotiating space.

So where is the obstacle?

The greater the potential, the more complex the diplomatic calculations. Bangladesh's first challenge is maintaining balance. Europe and North America are highly significant in the country’s exports, development cooperation, and financial system.

On the other hand, China, India, Japan, the Middle East, and other Asian countries are deeply connected to Bangladesh's economic and strategic interests. Therefore, if joining BRICS is presented as Bangladesh's geopolitical leaning towards one side, unnecessary diplomatic pressure could arise.

The second challenge lies within BRICS itself. The interests of its members are not identical in all areas. There is competition between China and India; a deep hostility exists between Russia and the Western world; the security priorities of Iran and other Middle Eastern countries are not the same.

Amidst such diversity, it is yet to be determined how coherent a political power BRICS will become.

Thirdly, membership itself is no guarantee of economic success. Simply joining an alliance does not automatically increase investment, trade, or development financing.

Bangladesh's diplomatic success will be achieved when Dhaka deepens its relationship with Beijing without losing Washington, maintains cooperation with Delhi while preserving its strategic independence, works with Moscow without endangering its market in Brussels, and becomes close with BRICS without presenting itself to other partners as a follower of any geopolitical camp.

For that, a clear national strategy, project preparation capacity, commercial planning, and skilled economic diplomacy are necessary.

Whether Bangladesh should join BRICS is not so straightforward. The more important question is how Bangladesh will use BRICS to serve its national interests. Membership in international organisations is not an ornament; it is a tool.

If the goal of entering BRICS is simply to achieve a new identity, its value is limited. However, if through this Bangladesh can achieve infrastructure financing, new markets, energy security, investment, technology cooperation, and a stronger voice on the political stage of the broader South, then its strategic value is much higher.

Today's world no longer revolves around a single centre. Power is spreading, new poles are forming, and alongside old alliances, new equations are arising.

In this changing world, Bangladesh does not need to choose one camp; it needs to increase the value of its position. BRICS is one of those opportunities.

Bangladesh's diplomatic success will be achieved when Dhaka deepens its relationship with Beijing without losing Washington, maintains cooperation with Delhi while preserving its strategic independence, works with Moscow without endangering its market in Brussels, and becomes close with BRICS without presenting itself to other partners as a follower of any geopolitical camp.

Because the greatest strength of small and medium-sized states is not always their military capability—often, their greatest strength is the diplomatic ability to become necessary to all rather than being someone's satellite state or dependent country.

For Bangladesh, BRICS could be a way to enhance that capability—if membership is seen as a means to achieve national interest, not as an end goal.

item.title: Police want AI cameras to curb yaba, how will these work?
item.description:
Yaba enters Bangladesh after being smuggled across the Myanmar border. From there, it is transported through hilly trails, old roads, and alternative routes to Cox’s Bazar town and various other parts of the country. To evade surveillance by law enforcement agencies along the border, smugglers frequently change routes and employ new tactics. As a result, although yaba shipments are intercepted at the border, its spread has not been stopped.

For this reason, the police have taken an initiative to monitor the long route used to smuggle yaba from the border to urban areas. A proposal has been made to establish permanent checkpoints at 11 key locations in Cox’s Bazar and Bandarban. These checkpoints will be equipped with artificial intelligence (AI)-powered facial recognition cameras, CCTV cameras, drug-detection dog squads, and vehicle and luggage scanners.

A total of 321 police personnel have been requested to operate the checkpoints. The estimated cost for equipment and infrastructure is approximately Tk 13 crore (Tk 130 million). The Chattogram Range Police sent the proposal to police headquarters on July 27.

The proposal was prepared by Md. Nazimul Haque, Additional Deputy Inspector General of the Chattogram Range, after visiting the border areas of Cox’s Bazar and Bandarban. He told Prothom Alo that the proposal was drawn up with the goal of ensuring that yaba is not allowed to enter the country under any circumstances.

Md. Nazimul Haque said suspected yaba dealers would be stopped and searched at the checkpoints. If they are not identified there, the AI cameras will be used to identify them. Photographs of the dealers and their associates will be stored in the system. As soon as they enter the area, the cameras will identify them. Drugs hidden in vehicles and luggage will be detected by scanners. If drugs still cannot be detected on someone, the dog squad will then be deployed.

Surveillance from the border to the city

Law enforcement agencies have conducted numerous operations to prevent drug trafficking. Even so, they have been unable to stop yaba from entering the country. From 2025 through July of this year, the Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) seized 15,134,945 yaba tablets, while the Department of Narcotics Control seized 43,562,811 tablets.

According to a report submitted by the Chattogram Range DIG, yaba enters Bangladesh from Myanmar’s Rakhine State through the Naf River, by sea routes, and through various points along the border. The Ukhia and Teknaf border areas of Cox’s Bazar and Naikhongchhari in Bandarban have been identified as key entry points for yaba.

However, police believe that monitoring the border alone will not be enough to stop the drug. After crossing the border, yaba is transported using alternative roads and hilly routes. Police plan to establish permanent checkpoints at points where these routes connect with major roads.

For this purpose, seven locations in Ramu, Cox’s Bazar Sadar, Ukhia and Chakaria in Cox’s Bazar, and four locations in Naikhongchhari, Bandarban, have been selected. The proposed locations include Rangkut Buddhist Monastery and the Ponero Chhara Forest Office in Ramu; Bhangar Mor, Chaufaldandi Iron Bridge and the railway station in Cox’s Bazar; Court Bazar Road in Ukhia; and Harbang Road in Chakaria. In Naikhongchhari, the proposed locations are Bailey Bridge, Sonachhari Chaurasta intersection, Baishari Petan Alipara intersection, and the Dakbanglo intersection in Ramu’s Gorjania.

Bhangar Mor to have the largest checkpoint

Of the 11 proposed checkpoints, Bhangar Mor has been identified as the most important. The location is at the end of Marine Drive. Police plan to establish extensive surveillance there to prevent yaba from reaching Cox’s Bazar town and the tourist areas.

The proposal calls for 42 police personnel to be stationed there. They will work in three shifts and include three sub-inspectors (SIs), three assistant sub-inspectors (ASIs), 29 male constables and seven female constables.
The checkpoint is proposed to have one dog squad, one luggage scanner, one vehicle scanner, three AI-powered facial-recognition cameras and 15 CCTV cameras. The proposal also estimates Tk 1.7 million for constructing a 500-square-foot semi-permanent building and an RCC parking pavement.

Old roads also under surveillance

Police also want to bring old yaba-trafficking routes under surveillance, rather than focusing only on the main roads.

The Ponero Chhara Forest Office–Katiar Matha area in Ukhia has been identified as an important route. According to the police proposal, traffickers have a tendency to use old roads to transport drugs from Teknaf and Ukhia to Cox’s Bazar. A 33-member checkpoint has therefore been proposed for the area.

The Rangkut Buddhist Monastery area in Ramu has also been deemed important. Police believe this point could help prevent drugs arriving via the road that branches off from the Marichya checkpoint and from the hilly areas.

Meanwhile, the Dakbanglo intersection in Gorjania has been identified as important because it is a four-way junction surrounded by remote, forested hill areas.

In other words, the central strategy of the police plan is to prevent drugs from reaching cities or other parts of the country after entering through the border. To achieve this, surveillance zones will be established at every important junction where routes from the border connect to major roads.

Three checkpoints in Naikhongchhari

The proposal gives particular importance to Naikhongchhari in Bandarban. Because of the risk of drugs being transported through small hilly roads near the border, three permanent checkpoints have been proposed there: Bailey Bridge, the Chaurasta intersection in Sonachhari union, and the Baishari Petan Alipara intersection.

Each checkpoint is proposed to have 33 police personnel. The Baishari Petan Alipara intersection is about 22 kilometers from Naikhongchhari Police Station. This hilly junction could become an important route for transporting drugs.

Meanwhile, the Sonachhari Chaurasta is where four roads meet. Police believe it would therefore be comparatively easy to stop and inspect vehicles there.

Traffickers to be caught on camera

The Chattogram Range Police do not plan to rely solely on police personnel to guard the 11 checkpoints; they also want to bring them under technological surveillance.

According to the proposal, a total of 31 AI-based facial-recognition cameras and 140 regular CCTV cameras will be installed at the checkpoints. Photographs of suspected yaba dealers and their associates will be stored in the AI system. The plan is for the cameras to identify them as soon as they enter the coverage area of a checkpoint.

The system will also include six vehicle-scanning machines and eight luggage scanners.

Each of the six vehicle scanners is estimated to cost Tk 15.5 million, for a total of Tk 93 million. Each of the eight luggage scanners is estimated to cost Tk 4.5 million, bringing their total cost to Tk 36 million.

The proposal also estimates Tk 500,000 for AI-based facial-detection software and Tk 2.852 million for 23 65-inch televisions.

In other words, technology accounts for a major portion of the proposal. Police believe these technologies will help reduce the opportunity for traffickers to evade detection by concealing drugs in vehicles or luggage.

If one route closes, another is found

Akhtar Kabir Chowdhury, secretary of Citizens for Good Governance (SUJAN) Chattogram, has stressed that combating drugs requires not only law enforcement operations but also shutting down trafficking routes. He told Prothom Alo that while law enforcement operations are necessary to control drugs, it is equally important to close the routes used to transport them. He said the proposed technological measures should therefore be implemented quickly.

Akhtar Kabir Chowdhury said that when one route is closed, traffickers look for another. Coordinated surveillance is needed everywhere, including the border, hilly routes, alternative roads, railway lines and entry points into cities. Without integrated monitoring, it will not be possible to completely shut down the routes used by smugglers.

A call was made to Additional DIG Mahbubul Karim’s mobile phone to inquire about the progress of the proposal sent to police headquarters, but he did not respond. As a result, there is still no confirmed information about whether the proposal will be implemented.

If the police proposal is implemented, however, multiple surveillance zones will be established along the yaba-trafficking routes beyond the border. The main objective of the system will be to intercept yaba shipments after they enter Bangladesh but before they reach the cities.

item.title: SSC results changed after re-scrutiny? Here’s how to apply for Class XI admission
item.description:
The revised results of Secondary School Certificate (SSC) and equivalent examinations following re-scrutiny have been incorporated into the Class XI admission application portal (xiclassadmission.gov.bd). This was announced in a notice on the Class XI admission application portal on Friday (11 September 2026).

According to the notice, students whose results have changed following re-scrutiny can now apply, if they have not already done so, or modify applications they have already submitted. This year, online applications for Class XI admission will remain open until 8:00 pm on 13 September. Those who failed to apply online by 10 September can also apply during this period. Applicants will have the opportunity to change their order of preference until 8:00 pm on 12 and 13 September.

Students can apply online by following the detailed guidelines provided on the admission website. Depending on their eligibility, a student can apply to a minimum of five and a maximum of ten colleges or equivalent educational institutions. The application fee is Tk 220.

SSC re-scrutiny results: 4,085 students pass, 3,079 more get GPA 5

What is needed to apply—

Before starting the application, students should keep several pieces of information at hand, including their SSC or equivalent examination roll number, registration number, name of the education board, year of passing, an active mobile phone number, a list of preferred colleges and information about the group they wish to enrol in. Before submitting the application, students should carefully check that all personal and examination information has been entered correctly.

The admission policy states that there will be no selection or admission test. Admission will be based solely on students’ SSC and equivalent examination results. Seven per cent of Class XI admission seats have been reserved under quotas. The remaining 93 per cent of the total seats at colleges will be open to all students on the basis of merit.

College admission applications open: How to apply

Important dates—

Students who receive their re-scrutiny or re-evaluation results between 2 and 13 September will also be able to apply. Applications from students whose results changed following re-scrutiny or re-evaluation will be accepted until 8:00 pm on 12 and 13 September. Applicants will also be able to change their order of preference until 8:00 pm on 12 and 13 September.

The results of selected students will be published at 8:00 pm on 17 September. After the results are published, selected students will have until 8:00 pm on 19 September to confirm their admission. If admission is not confirmed within the stipulated time, the selection and application will be cancelled. The Class XI admission process will take place from 20 to 22 September. Classes for Class XI will begin on 23 September.

item.title: Lawyer’s body recovered from Lalbagh
item.description:
Police recovered the partially decomposed body of a lawyer from a rented apartment in Lalbagh, Dhaka, on Saturday.
The deceased was Muhammad Anwar Hossain.
The body was recovered around 11:30am from the second floor of a house at 10/1, Lane 3, Bowbazar in Shahidnagar, under Lalbagh police station.
According to police, a tenant living in an adjacent room found Hossain lying dead and informed police.
Police from Lalbagh police station went to the scene and began the initial legal procedures. Members of the Criminal Investigation Department (CID) crime scene unit later arrived at the scene.
Hossain was a lawyer at the Dhaka Judge Court and had a chamber in Room 214 on the first floor of the Annex Building of the Dhaka Bar Association.
Police said Hossain lived alone in the rented house as a bachelor, while his family resides in his village home.
Lalbagh police station Officer-in-Charge (OC) Mohammad Jamil Hossain said Hossain lived alone.
“The initial suspicion is that he died of a stroke, and the body was 2 to 3 days old,” he said.
Police recovered his driving licence and are trying to contact his family after verifying the document.

item.title: Developing nations must work together
item.description:
With September 12 marking the UN Day for South-South Cooperation, Bangladesh must recognize the importance of cooperation among developing countries and actively work to strengthen its ties.
Indeed, it would not be a mistake to argue that most meaningful development partnerships increasingly lie within the Global South.
This day reflects a shift in global power, knowledge, and innovation. Developing nations now generate a substantial share of global growth, and their collective experience offers solutions far more relevant to our realities than traditional models originating in the developed North.
Bangladesh has repeatedly benefited from exchanges with fellow developing nations, be they agricultural techniques, disaster‑management expertise, digital‑governance models, renewable‑energy solutions, or public health innovations.
It goes without saying that solutions have greater odds of success when there is an exchange of context‑appropriate tools shaped by countries that have confronted similar constraints and pressures.
It must also be stated that Bangladesh is not merely a recipient, and its achievements in community‑based health systems, microfinance, disaster preparedness, and social‑protection programs have become global references for other nations in the Global South.
South-South cooperation allows Bangladesh to share these strengths while gaining new approaches to emerging challenges such as climate shocks, rapid urbanization, food insecurity, and digital transformation.
Given the importance, it is imperative that we deepen this engagement. Too often, cooperation remains limited to conferences, pilot projects, or symbolic agreements.
Bangladesh needs long‑term partnerships, ones that expand joint research, strengthen climate resilience, and reduce dependence on external models that do not align with our local realities.
The Global South’s collective future depends on how effectively its members learn from one another and build systems rooted in solidarity rather than hierarchy.
This cooperation could be a central pillar of a fairer, more resilient future for all of us.

item.title: PM to distribute 7,000 farmer cards in Feni on Thursday
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman will distribute 7000 farmers' cards in Feni on September 17, as the government has set a target to distribute 16.5 million cards among farmers over the next four years, with an estimated initial cost of Taka 681 crore.
Fisheries, Livestock and Agriculture minister Mohammad Amin Ur Rashid said this after visiting Fulgazi government Pilot High School playground, where the prime minister will distribute the cards, on Saturday morning.
Under the target, the government will distribute the farmer cards among 1.10 lakh farmers across the country on that day.
Simultaneous launching ceremonies will be held in 50 districts on the same day. Bank accounts have already been opened for one lakh of the 16.30 lakh farmers registered under the program so far, ministry officials said.
Under the cash incentive program, landless, marginal and small farmers holding the card will receive Tk2,500 directly through their bank accounts. Around one lakh farmers are expected to receive the incentive on the inauguration day.
Information on another five lakh farmers has already been verified and approved for opening bank accounts, the ministry said.
“The farmer cards will be distributed in each upazila and union, and the card will be distributed among all the farmers within the scheduled time”, the minister told the function.
The government has decided to bring farmers under the card system to make subsidies, loans, and incentives more accessible to them in the agriculture sector.
Regarding the fertilizer stock, the agriculture minister said the country has no crisis of fertilizer, as a ‘vicious circle’ is trying to create anarchy in the fertilizer distribution system.
The program will be implemented in three stages – pre-pilot, pilot and nationwide expansion. In the pre-pilot phase, farmers engaged in crop production, fisheries and livestock, including dairy farmers, will be included across 11 blocks in 11 upazilas of 10 districts.
According to the ministry, the pre-pilot phase of the Farmer's Card distribution program has already been launched on Pohela Boishakh, the first day of the Bangla New Year on April 14 this year.
In the first phase, 22,065 farmers in 11 upazilas under 10 districts received the cards. Of them, 20,671 landless, marginal, and small farmers received Tk2,500 annually in direct cash assistance.
The Agriculture Ministry aims to distribute Farmer Cards to 43 lakh farmers during the 2026-27 fiscal year, out of an estimated 2.27 crore farmers nationwide.
The remaining farmers will gradually be brought under the program, according to the ministry.
Additional Secretary of the agriculture ministry Md Yasin, Director General of the Department of Agricultural Extension (DAE) Md Abdur Rahim, Deputy Commissioner of Feni Mohammad Mahbubul Karim, Fulgazi Upazila Nirbahi Officer Md Kawser Hamid, Fulgazi Upazila assistant commissioner (land) Soheli Nawshin Protasha, BNP national executive committee assistant secretary Belal Hossen, BNP national executive committee member Abu Taleb, and Upazila BNP convener Fakhrul Alam Swapan were also present during this time.

item.title: Bobby Hajjaj: Govt to align Bangla, English-medium curricula with global standards
item.description:
The government will bring necessary changes to the Bangla- and English-medium curricula to bring Bangladesh’s education system up to global standards, State Minister for Primary and Mass Education Bobby Hajjaj has said. He made the remarks while addressing the School Leaders Conference 2026, organised by OxfordAQA International Qualifications, at a hotel in the capital on Saturday.
Hajjaj said the government would work with both public and private educational institutions to coordinate efforts in curriculum development, infrastructure, teacher training and technology use.
“We do not want merely to follow the world’s best practices. Our dream is that one day other countries will look to Bangladesh for best practices in education,” he said, adding that the government was prepared to invest the necessary time, resources and effort to achieve the goal.
He said students studying in English-medium, Bangla-medium or other streams should have a common standard of basic knowledge and skills.
“There will be differences between better and less-performing institutions, but there should not be major disparities in the fundamental quality of education and curriculum,” he said.
Highlighting the need for urgent reforms in primary education, the state minister said clear minimum standards should be set for school hours and effective learning hours, student numbers relative to classroom capacity, essential infrastructure and trained teachers.
“No teacher should be assigned to a classroom without proper training,” he said.
Emphasising technology and modern teaching methods, Hajjaj said future primary education would place greater emphasis on activity-based and play-based learning.
He said the government also wanted to learn from the experience of English-medium schools and make effective use of learning management systems (LMS).
Stressing the importance of stakeholder consultation in developing a new curriculum, Hajjaj said, “We do not want anyone to say they were not consulted. We want to move forward by taking your experience and views into account.”
He said the government was working to create a level playing field for all educational institutions through coordinated initiatives in four areas—curriculum, infrastructure, teacher training and technology.
OxfordAQA Bangladesh and Nepal Country Director Shaheen Reza chaired the event, while University Grants Commission (UGC) member Professor Dr Abdullah Al Mamun attended as a special guest.

item.title: Bangladesh U-20 women’s hockey team beat Malaysia to clinch fifth spot at Junior Asia Cup
item.description:
Bangladesh concluded their campaign in the 2026 Women’s Junior Asia Cup hockey tournament with a 2-1 victory over Malaysia in Hulunbuir City, Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region, China, on Saturday.
The victory in their final match secured Bangladesh fifth place — their best-ever finish in the competition.
The women in red and green started strongly and displayed excellent hockey from the outset, but neither team managed to find the net in the first half.
Bangladesh finally broke the deadlock in the third quarter when captain Sharika Rimon converted a penalty stroke in the 31st minute.
Kona Akter then doubled Bangladesh’s lead with a superb field goal in the 50th minute.
Malaysia pulled a goal back late in the match through Irdina Jefrey in the 59th minute, but Bangladesh held on to secure a memorable victory.
The result capped an impressive campaign for Bangladesh, who began the tournament with a 7-0 victory over Chinese Taipei before thrashing Pakistan 5-1, Kazakhstan 4-0 and Hong Kong China 6-0 to finish as unbeaten champions of the Challengers Group.
Bangladesh then suffered a 2-0 defeat to strong Japan in the quarterfinals, sending them into the fifth-place playoff, where they overcame Malaysia to finish fifth.
The result marks Bangladesh’s best-ever performance in the Women’s Junior Asia Cup, improving on their ninth-place finish in their maiden appearance in the competition in 2024.

item.title: Miraz continues to impress in CPL
item.description:
Bangladesh allrounder Mehedi Hasan Miraz produced a yet another match-winning bowling performance to guide Guyana Amazon Warriors to a six-wicket victory over Trinbago Knight Riders in the Caribbean Premier League (CPL) at Providence Stadium.
Making his CPL debut in the previous match, Miraz had taken three wickets for just 13 runs.
He followed that up with an impressive four-wicket haul in his second appearance, earning the Player of the Match award as Guyana chased down a modest target with eight balls to spare.
Put into bat, Trinbago Knight Riders made a brisk start, reaching 41 in 4.3 overs before Miraz struck for the first time, bowling Colin Munro for 26 off 16 balls.
Imran Tahir, who had set a world record for the oldest player to claim a five-wicket haul at the age of 47 in the previous match, dismissed Alex Hales for 22.
Justin Greaves top-scored for Trinbago with 35 off 37 balls, but the rest of the batting lineup failed to offer much resistance.
Miraz then bowled Nicholas Pooran first ball before dismissing Gudakesh Motie and Sunil Narine to finish with four wickets for 23 runs from his four overs. Shamar Joseph claimed two wickets as Trinbago were restricted to 126-8 in 20 overs.
Guyana lost openers Mavendra Dindyal and Glenn Phillips for 36, but Shimron Hetmyer and Shai Hope steadied the innings and guided the hosts towards victory.
Hetmyer scored 42 off 35 balls, while Hope contributed 28 off 19 balls. Guyana reached 127-4 in 18.4 overs to secure their sixth-wicket victory.
Miraz, who came in late in the innings, scored just two runs off 14 balls, but his outstanding bowling performance had already laid the foundation for Guyana's comfortable win.
The victory kept Guyana Amazon Warriors at the top of the points table with 16 points from nine matches. Antigua and Barbuda Falcons are second with 13 points from 10 matches.

item.title: Nrityanchal celebrates 25th anniversary at Bangladesh Shilpakala Academy
item.description:
Nrityanchal Performing Arts Academy, one of Bangladesh’s leading dance institutions, celebrated its 25th anniversary with a three-day Silver Jubilee Festival from September 11 to 13 at the Bangladesh Shilpakala Academy.
The festivities commenced on September 11 with a rally on the Shilpakala Academy premises.
Legendary dancers and Directors of Nrityanchal, Shamim Ara Nipa and Shibli Mohammad, joined teachers, students, and crew members to officially launch the event by releasing balloons and festoons.
On September 12, a special children’s performance titled "Chhoray Chhonde Nrityamala" took place at the National Theater Hall. State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obayed attended as chief guest.
The ceremony featured guest appearances by Sheikh Rezauddin Stalin, director general of Bangladesh Shilpakala Academy, along with eminent dance maestros Amanul Huq, Kajal Ibrahim, Lubna Marium, Soma Mumtaz, Belayet Hossain Khan, and Anisul Islam Hero, who joined the co-founders to mark the inauguration.
Choreographed by Shamim Ara Nipa under the supervision of Shibli Mohammad, the production featured over 400 young students performing dance routines based on educational rhymes.
The festival concluded on September 13 with "Nrityamalika," graced by Minister of Cultural Affairs Nitai Roy Chowdhury as chief guest.
More than 300 artists, alongside senior performers, showcased folk, creative, and classical dance pieces.
A key highlight of the final evening was a performance by duo Shamim Ara Nipa and Shibli Mohammad, celebrating 25 years of artistic leadership.
Throughout September 12 and 13, an exhibition in the lobby showcased photographs, memorabilia, and milestones spanning Nrityanchal's 25-year journey.
Maasranga Television served as the official media partner, with support from Shah Cement.
A video was uploaded on YouTube that highlighted traditional Bangladeshi group dance choreography, complementing the rich performing arts heritage celebrated during Nrityanchal's silver jubilee.

item.title: Bank Asia signs agreement with BB for CMSME working capital refinance fund
item.description:

The agreement signing ceremony was held on September 8, at the AN Hamidullah Conference Room at the Bangladesh Bank head office.
Md Anis Ur Rahman, deputy governor of Bangladesh Bank, attended the ceremony as chief guest.
Md Zabdul Islam, director of the SME & Special Programs Department of Bangladesh Bank and Syed Zulkar Nayen, deputy managing director of Bank Asia, exchanged agreement documents on behalf of their respective organizations.
Nahid Rahman, executive director, Shahanaj Pervin, additional director of Bangladesh Bank, and Mohammad Saifuddowla, head of small business of Bank Asia, were also present.
The fund has been established by Bangladesh Bank under the Tk60,000 crore stimulus package. The initiative aims to provide necessary working capital loans/investment to CMSME enterprises, enabling them to operate their production, service and business activities at full capacity.
It is also expected to contribute to creating direct and indirect employment and help accelerate the country’s economic recovery.
Under this fund, generally viable CMSME enterprises that are unable to operate at full capacity due to a shortage of working capital will be eligible for financing at an interest rate of 9%.

item.title: Prime Bank joins BB’s Tk5,000cr working capital refinance fund for CMSMEs
item.description:
Prime Bank PLC has signed a participation agreement with Bangladesh Bank to join its Tk5,000 crore Working Capital Refinance Fund for the CMSME sector, aimed at providing working capital financing to eligible CMSME enterprises at affordable interest rates and on easier terms.
The agreement was signed recently at the AN Hamidullah Conference Room at Bangladesh Bank head office.
Md Jabdul Islam, director, SME & Special Programs Department, Bangladesh Bank and M Nazeem A Choudhury, additional managing director, Prime Bank PLC, signed the agreement on behalf of their respective organizations.
Md Anisur Rahman, deputy governor of Bangladesh Bank, attended the signing ceremony as chief guest.
Nahid Rahman, executive director, and Shahanaj Parveen, additional director, Bangladesh Bank, were also present at the event.
The refinance fund has been established under Bangladesh Bank’s Tk60,000 crore stimulus package to provide necessary working capital loans/investment to CMSMEs, enabling them to operate their production, service and business activities at full capacity.
The initiative also aims to create direct and indirect employment opportunities and contribute to revitalizing economic activity in the country.
Under the scheme, eligible operational CMSME enterprises that are unable to run their production, service or business activities at full capacity due to a shortage of working capital will have access to financing at an interest rate of up to 9%.
Prime Bank has been supporting the growth of the CMSME sector through financing and tailored solutions for entrepreneurs.
By participating in the refinance fund, the bank aims to further expand access to affordable working capital financing for CMSME businesses, helping them strengthen operations, enhance production capacity, sustain business growth and contribute to employment generation.

item.title: BB backtracks from reducing profit on deposits of Sammilito Islami Bank
item.description:
Bangladesh Bank has stepped back from its previous "haircut" decision to reduce profit calculations for depositors of Sammilito Islami Bank, which was formed by merging five banks.
As a result, instead of providing profit at a fixed rate of 4%, deposit accounts will be recalculated according to the bank's effective profit rate during the relevant period.
This directive was issued on Thursday (September 10) in a letter signed by Shams Tabriz Bhuiyan, additional director of the Bank Resolution Department of Bangladesh Bank.
According to the new instructions, profit for personal or non-institutional term deposits and installment-based deposits from January 1, 2024, to December 28, 2025, will no longer be fixed at a 4% rate.
Each deposit account must be reassessed taking into account the effective profit rate of the bank during that period.
In addition, the bank's recalculated profit rate will apply for an interim period of three days from December 29 to December 31, 2025.
The Bangladesh Bank letter stated that the previous haircut instructions were reconsidered to restore depositor confidence, ensure the long-term stability of the bank, and address the practical complexities of profit adjustment.
Consequently, profit for personal term and installment depositors for that period will no longer be calculated at a uniform 4%.
Instead, each account balance must be recalculated based on the effective profit rate of that time.
With this decision, the previous measure to limit personal depositors' profit to 4% at Sammilito Islami Bank has effectively been cancelled.
Depositors' dues will now be recalculated based on the bank's effective profit rate during the specified period.
