item.title: Four killed in accident while returning from wedding in Chittagong
item.description:
Four people were killed and eight others injured in a head-on collision between a covered van and a microbus in Karnaphuli, Chittagong, while they were returning home after attending a wedding ceremony.
Two of the deceased died at the scene, while the other two succumbed to their injuries after being taken to hospital, police said.
The accident occurred around 2am on Sunday in the College Bazar area of Karnaphuli on the Chittagong-Cox’s Bazar Highway.
According to witnesses, the covered van had crossed the Shah Amanat Bridge and was making a high-speed U-turn in the College Bazar area when it collided with the microbus coming from the opposite direction.
The deceased were identified as Niaz Morshed, 22, his younger sister Mimtah, 17, their maternal uncle Md Ferdous Alam, 55, and microbus driver Md Munna. All of them were residents of Eidgah area in Cox’s Bazar.
Seven of the injured were admitted to Chittagong Medical College Hospital.
Police and eyewitnesses said Mimtah’s elder sister’s wedding was held at a community centre in Agrabad, Chittagong city, on Saturday night. After the ceremony, several family members and relatives were returning to Eidgah in Cox’s Bazar in the microbus when the accident occurred.
Nur Ahmad, officer-in-charge of Karnaphuli police station, told Bangla Tribune that four people died in the accident—two at the scene and two after being taken to hospital.
“The covered van has been seized following the accident, but its driver and assistant fled the scene. Legal action is being taken,” he said.
SI Nurul Alam Ashik of the Chittagong Medical College Hospital police outpost said the accident occurred around 2am in the College Bazar area under Karnaphuli police station.
He said the injured were taken to the hospital.

item.title: Prominent Urdu poet Syed Taqi Mohammad dies
item.description:
Syed Taqi Mohammad, also known as Buddan Saheb, a distinguished Urdu poet and prominent social worker and organiser from Old Dhaka, has died at the age of 76.
He died around 8pm Friday at his residence in the Sat Rawza area of Old Dhaka.
Journalist Tarun Sarkar confirmed the news to the media on Saturday in a press release issued on behalf of the Committee for Commissioning Books on Architecture (Dhakar Sthapotto Bishoyok Grontho Pronoyon Committee).
Syed Taqi Mohammad is survived by his wife and five children.
His namaz-e-janaza was held on Saturday afternoon after Zuhr prayers at Hussaini Dalan Imambara. He was later buried at the family graveyard in Sat Rawza.
Born on January 14, 1950, Syed Taqi Mohammad belonged to an aristocratic Mughal family in Sat Rawza. His father, Nawab Syed Ali Mohammad, known as Chhotton, was a prominent zamindar of Dhaka.
Throughout his life, Syed Taqi Mohammad held leadership positions in various social and cultural organisations. He was a member of the Hussaini Dalan Management Committee and the National Waqf Committee.
He also served as mutawalli of the Mohammadi Beg Imambara Waqf Estate, established in Old Dhaka during the Mughal era, until his death.
The kulkhani (post-funeral prayer) for the deceased will be held on Monday. The first session will take place at Hussaini Dalan after Maghrib prayers, followed by a second session at Sat Rawza Khaja Nehal Mosque after Isha prayers.
Tarun Sarkar said Syed Taqi Mohammad had assisted the Committee for Commissioning Books on Architecture by providing important information and documents for its survey of the city’s inscriptions and architectural heritage.

item.title: Man’s dismembered body found in six pieces in three sacks
item.description:
Police have recovered the dismembered body of an unidentified man, cut into six pieces and packed into three plastic sacks, from beside a paddy field in Madhukhali, Faridpur.
The remains were recovered around 10am Saturday from an area near Boalia Stand in Boalia union of the upazila.
According to police and local sources, passersby spotted three tied plastic sacks at the base of a palm tree beside paddy fields belonging to Lavlu Mallick and Ishaq Miah. The sacks were found on the right side of the Faridpur-bound road, about 200 yards past Boalia Stand.
Suspecting something was wrong, locals called the national emergency service number 999. An assistant superintendent of police for the Madhukhali-Boalmari-Alphadanga circle and Sub-Inspector Masudur Rahman of Madhukhali police station later arrived at the scene with a team.
The sacks were opened in the presence of locals, revealing six severed body parts believed to be those of a man aged around 40.
Police prepared an inquest report at the scene, but the man’s identity could not immediately be established.
Masuduzzaman, ASP of the Madhukhali-Boalmari-Alphadanga circle, said the remains had been sent to Faridpur Medical College Hospital for an autopsy.
“If the identity remains unknown after the autopsy, necessary arrangements will be made to hand the body over to Anjuman Mufidul Islam for burial in accordance with religious rites,” he said.
He added that police were working to identify the deceased and determine the circumstances behind the incident.
Further legal proceedings are underway.

item.title: Complaint filed with tribunal seeking justice for Sagar-Runi murder
item.description:
A formal complaint has been filed with the Office of the Chief Prosecutor of the International Crimes Tribunal seeking justice for the murders of journalist couple Sagar Sarowar and Meherun Runi.
Runi’s brother, Naosher Roman, submitted the complaint to Chief Prosecutor Md Aminul Islam on Sunday.
According to the complaint, Sagar Sarowar, news editor of Maasranga Television, and Meherun Runi, a senior correspondent at ATN Bangla, were murdered in their rented apartment in the capital’s West Rajabazar area between 2am and 7am on February 11, 2012.
Despite the passage of 14 years, multiple investigative agencies have failed to identify the perpetrators or make significant progress in the case, the complaint said.
It said local police, the Detective Branch (DB) and the Rapid Action Battalion (RAB) had failed to make progress after the murders. The High Court subsequently directed the Police Bureau of Investigation (PBI) to take over the case.
However, even after the PBI investigation, the case remains unresolved, according to the complaint.
The family has therefore sought a fair and proper investigation through the International Crimes Tribunal to identify the perpetrators and bring them to justice.
The complaint also sought exemplary punishment for those responsible and requested that it be formally registered so that legal proceedings can be initiated.

item.title: Zubaida: Govt takes initiatives to ensure healthcare for marginalised communities
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman’s wife and Ziaur Rahman Foundation Vice Chairman Dr Zubaida Rahman has said the government has taken various initiatives to ensure healthcare reaches people in the most marginalised communities.
She made the remarks at a seminar titled “Innovation in Healthcare for All” at the Innovation Fair at Novo Theatre in Bijoy Sarani, Dhaka, on Sunday morning.
“Healthcare is not charity; it is a fundamental right,” Dr Zubaida said.
She pointed to a communication gap between researchers and healthcare providers, saying closer collaboration between the two could improve the quality of healthcare.
She also stressed the need to expand awareness programmes on cancer and diabetes.
Dr Zubaida said Bangladesh could ensure world-class healthcare by strengthening coordination between technology and researchers.
She said the government plans to restructure the health sector so that it can contribute 5% to the country’s GDP in the future.
Speaking at the event, State Minister for Health Dr MA Muhit said innovations in dengue prevention should be tested and implemented in Bangladesh.
He called for initiatives to bring Bangladeshi scientists working abroad back home and utilise their expertise.
The state minister also stressed the need to introduce a digital platform for appointment booking at all government hospitals.

item.title: England survive scare to seal 3-0 sweep against Pakistan
item.description:
Joe Root led from the front as England survived a major wobble to beat Pakistan by eight wickets in the third Test at Edgbaston on Saturday, sealing a 3-0 series whitewash.
The home team, chasing just 130 to win, were in deep trouble when openers Ben Duckett and Emilio Gay were dismissed in the first over, bowled by Mohammad Abbas.
Root, England's record runscorer, edged his first ball, bowled by Razaullah, through the slips for four in a nervy start but settled and scored quickly to take the sting out of the situation.
The captain was given a huge reprieve when he chopped onto the stumps off Mohammad Ali, only for the umpire to signal a no ball, leaving the bowler distraught.
Root, with Jordan Cox at the other end, had another let-off when he edged an Abbas delivery between first and second slip, with neither fielder moving.
But he reached his half-century off 57 balls with a cut for four and Cox reached the landmark shortly afterwards.
England reached their target in the 25th over, with Root unbeaten on 62 and Cox 59 not out.
Root, in his second spell as England skipper after the departure of Ben Stokes, admitted his team were not the finished article but said he was delighted with their series win.
"The amount of uncertainty, noise and I guess chaos there was coming into the series, the way the guys have dealt with that -- being so clinical with what we've had in front of us -- and be stood here with a 3-0 win is really pleasing," he told Sky Sports.
"It sets us up nicely looking ahead to the start of a new era with (new head coach) Stephen Fleming coming in."
England celebrated their first Test series win since 2024 while Pakistan have now lost 16 of their past 21 games and are rooted at the bottom of the World Test Championship table.
Root's men had appeared set for a quickfire win inside three days on Friday before debutant fast bowler Razaullah launched an audacious assault with the bat, clubbing nine sixes as he raced to 81 off 63 balls.
The 21-year-old number nine, who also took four wickets in England's first innings, put on 121 for the ninth wicket with fellow paceman Abbas (42) as England floundered.
"We had a little bit of pushback yesterday which, in a strange way, was quite a good thing for the group," said Root.
"Fair play to Razaullah, he made things difficult for us. He played some wonderful shots and made it very difficult to set fields to. He struck the ball nicely -- I don't know how he didn't pull a muscle, swinging the bat that hard."
Razaullah's heroics have changed the mood music but they came too little, too late for Pakistan, who have endured a miserable series, losing the first Test by an innings and 103 runs and the second by 194 runs.
The tourists sent seven players home after their crushing defeat in the second Test at Lord's and brought in seven replacements, with Razaullah among them.
They also sacked head coach Sarfaraz Ahmed and assistant Umar Gul as their tour plunged into chaos.
Pakistan made four changes to their side for the third Test in Birmingham and they put up a fight despite being dismissed for a paltry 133 in their first innings.
Captain Babar Azam admitted his team would have to take stock after a one-sided series.
"Before we came here we had to think about different things and to decide our team," he said.
"We had a couple of changes after losing two matches. Playing in England is very difficult. We were trying to do our best in the third match.
"We need to sit down and look hard at our mistakes, decide our playing XI."
The 3-0 win is a huge tonic for England, who were in turmoil just weeks ago following a series loss to New Zealand and the exits of head coach Brendon McCullum and Stokes.
But tougher challenges lie ahead, starting with a Test series in South Africa in December and January, while a home Ashes looms next year.

item.title: Messi scores but Miami held by Nashville
item.description:
Lionel Messi extended his incredible scoring streak against MLS-leaders Nashville on Saturday as Inter Miami battled to a 2-2 draw in their top-of-the-table Eastern Conference clash.
Messi curled in a superb strike on 62 minutes at Miami's Nu Stadium to fire Inter into a 2-1 lead but Nashville grabbed a share of the points after striker Sam Surridge bundled in an injury-time equaliser.
The 39-year-old Messi has now scored a remarkable 17 goals in 14 games against Nashville in all competitions since joining Miami in 2023.
And Messi could have even improved his goals record against in Saturday's game between the first and second-placed sides in the Eastern Conference.
Messi saw a shot crash off the underside of the bar in the 50th minute and also saw a shot cannon off the post in the 78th minute. A late Messi effort was also headed clear by Nashville defender Jeisson Palacios before Surridge's leveler.
The result leaves Inter nine points adrift of Nashville in the race for top seeding with nine regular season games remaining.
Earlier, Nashville had got off to a dream start when English striker Surridge sprang the offside trap before burying a low shot into the bottom corner in the fourth minute.
But Miami drew level midway through the half and again Messi was involved. The World Cup-winner's wicked in-swinging corner found the head of Nashville defender Reed Baker-Whiting, who glanced in an own goal.
It looked as if Messi had grabbed the winner midway through the second half when he combined with former Argentina international team-mate Rodrigo De Paul on the edge of the area before curling a shot beyond the dive of Brian Schwake.
But Miami's failure to extend their lead proved costly as Surridge scored from close range in injury time to steal a point.

item.title: Mbappe at the double as Real Madrid sink Rayo
item.description:
Kylian Mbappe struck twice to help Real Madrid smash Rayo Vallecano 4-1 on Saturday to pull level with Barcelona at the top of La Liga.
Jose Mourinho's side got back to winning ways after a defeat by Real Betis in their previous top- flight outing, with a convincing victory against neighbours Rayo. Jude Bellingham and Alvaro Carreras were also on target for Real Madrid, while Sergio Camello pulled one back for the visitors early in the second half.
Champions Barcelona visit Levante on Sunday looking to extend their 100 percent start to the campaign and restore their lead on Madrid.
Mourinho's side took a commanding three-goal lead against Rayo by half-time.
"(It was) fundamental to win, above all after losing the last game in La Liga," Mourinho told Real Madrid TV.
"We killed the game in the first half -- that's not easy, working like we did after the ChampionsLeague game, not just physically, but mentally."
Los Blancos took the lead from the penalty spot in the 14th minute after Florian Lejeune clumsily felled Carreras. Mbappe sent Rayo goalkeeper Emil Audero the wrong way.
The French forward helped create the second, after Lejeune gave the ball away under pressure from Vinicius Junior. Carreras exchanged passes with Mbappe and drilled home.
Handed a first start for Madrid, the club's record signing Yan Diomande cut inside from the right flank with a rapid dribble that left Rayo's defence scrambling but lashed his shot high and wide.
Bellingham notched Madrid's third goal and his third of the season after Vinicius charged down the left and cut the ball back for the England international, who has started the season in top form.
Mourinho defended Vinicius in midweek after some Madrid supporters whistled him in the Champions League win over Inter Milan.
Mbappe powered a strike from distance against the post as Madrid sought a fourth, while Pedro Diaz forced a rare save from Thibaut Courtois at the other end, the Belgian with a strong hand to push away his effort.
Diaz hit the post early in the second half as Rayo tried to find a foothold at the Santiago Bernabeu.
- Golden ambitions -
Mbappe, who stated his case for why he should win the Ballon d'Or this week, almost added a second with a low drive. Rayo pulled one back in the 51st minute when Vinicius gave the ball away to Camello under pressure and the forward poked past Courtois. It was the Spanish forward's sixth goal of the campaign, making him joint-top scorer with Barcelona's Raphinha and Mbappe.
Benat San Jose's side, 15th, had further chances to score but Courtois pushed out Giorgi Tsitaishvili's drive and an effort from Lejeune.
Mourinho brought on Turkish midfielder Arda Guler to help regain some control.
"Arda is very good, he's got a lot of quality, he influences the team's play in a good way and today he made a difference in terms of the stability of the game," said Mourinho.
Guler helped create Madrid's fourth for Mbappe in stoppage time, lethally finished low and across goal. It was Mbappe's seventh goal of the season across all competitions.
"Conceding the (early) penalty was a blow, then we had another mistake when bringing the ball out," said Rayo coach San Jose.
"I think we could have scored in the first half too, but it's true that they were better..."We have to congratulate Madrid, but I'm proud of the players because the second half was much better."
On Tuesday Real Madrid travel to face Elche, while Rayo Vallecano host Espanyol.Earlier on Saturday, Racing Santander defeated third-place Alaves 2-1, while Espanyol won 2-0 at Osasuna and Athletic Bilbao drew 1-1 at home against Elche.

item.title: Guimaraes strike lights up Arsenal win over Sunderland
item.description:
Bruno Guimaraes's brilliant first Arsenal goal and David Raya's penalty save inspired the Gunners to a 2-0 victory at Sunderland on Saturday to extend a flawless start to their Premier League title defence.
Mikel Arteta's men have conceded just once in five games in all competitions but Sunderland had the chance to breach Arsenal's imposing rearguard when Raya tipped Enzo Le Fee's spot-kick onto the post.
Just over two minutes later Guimaraes silenced the Stadium of Light as the Brazilian smashed into the top corner from outside the box.
Bukayo Saka's penalty sealed the victory with the final kick of the game after Sunderland defender Reinildo saw a second yellow card for taking down the England international.
Despite the victory Arteta was still seething after the game at the award of Sunderland's penalty for Ezri Konsa's pull on Dan Ballard.
"It is unacceptable at this level. Unacceptable!" Arteta said. "This can change the course of a season, the championshipm it is not acceptable."
The Arsenal boss added: "I've been in football for almost 28 years. It is not a penalty in any case, in any game, in any context, in any league."
Arsenal open up a three-point lead over Manchester City, who face local rivals Manchester United on Sunday, at the top of the table.
Their lead is already five ahead of Chelsea, six in front of Liverpool and eight clear of United as Arsenal threaten to run away with the title unless a new-look City under Enzo Maresca can keep pace.
Despite only winning by a single goal, Arsenal showed signs of blossoming into a more potent attacking force in statement wins over Chelsea last weekend and Napoli on Wednesday to get their Champions League campaign off to a flying start.
But the visitors had to rely on their organisation off the ball to grind out a vital three points as they failed to sparkle in attack but for a moment of magic from Guimaraes.
The former Newcastle captain was given a hostile reception on his arrival to the home of the Magpies' biggest rivals.
Guimaraes was Arsenal's big-money recruit of the transfer window, but the £75 million ($87 million) signing is yet to start for his new club as Arteta has kept faith with Myles Lewis-Skelly alongside Declan Rice and Martin Odegaard in midfield.
Kai Havertz came closest to breaking the deadlock of a cagey first half when his shot on the spin was tipped over by Robin Roefs.
Arteta made his move at the break by introducing Guimaraes for Lewis-Skelly, while Jurrien Timber also replaced the injured Ben White.
Sunderland are one of few sides capable of matching Arsenal's physicality and a set-piece wrestling match led to the penalty.
Konsa dragged Ballard to the ground although Arsenal argued it was the Sunderland defender who initiated contact.
Le Fee's effort was arrowed toward the bottom corner, but Raya produced a brilliant save to turn it onto the post.
From potentially being behind, Arsenal were in front 122 seconds later.
There appeared little danger when Rice fed Guimaraes, but he took aim and rifled a shot in off the underside of the bar.
Saka was denied a second by Roefs and Havertz saw a header cleared off the line by Ballard as Arsenal sought to put the game to bed.
They eventually did so deep into stoppage time when Reinildo brought down Saka in a desperate attempt to halt the winger's charge towards goal.
The Mozambique international was reduced to tears on his sorry trudge off the field.
Roefs nearly bailed out his teammate as he got a hand to Saka's penalty, but unlike Raya he failed to get enough on the ball to turn it wide.

item.title: Rybakina beats Sabalenka to win US Open title, takes No. 1 ranking
item.description:
Elena Rybakina defeated defending champion Aryna Sabalenka 6-4, 5-7, 6-2 on Saturday to win her first US Open title and complete her rise to the top of the women’s world rankings.
Rybakina had already secured the No. 1 ranking by reaching the semifinals, but capped her campaign by claiming the trophy Sabalenka had won in the previous two years.
“It’s still so difficult to process what happened,” Rybakina said. “Too many achievements these few weeks.”
The victory gave the 27-year-old her third Grand Slam title and second of the year. She also defeated Sabalenka in the Australian Open final earlier this season.
Rybakina ended Sabalenka’s 19-match winning streak at the US Open. Sabalenka had not lost at Flushing Meadows since the 2023 final against Coco Gauff.
Rybakina earned $5.5 million, the biggest prize in Grand Slam history, and joined Sabalenka and French Open champion Mirra Andreeva as the only players with three tour titles this season.
Sabalenka, who received $2.8 million, was seeking to become the first woman since Serena Williams from 2012-14 to win three consecutive US Open titles. She smashed her racket after briefly embracing Rybakina at the net.
“I was just out there competing, trying to do my best with what I had there today,” Sabalenka said. “Not good enough.”
Although Rybakina struggled with her first serve, she consistently pressured Sabalenka with her returns. She earned 12 break points and converted three, enough to secure the victory.
Rybakina’s win was the first time the lower-ranked player prevailed in a US Open women’s final between the No. 1 and No. 2 seeds since 2000.
Sabalenka had occupied the top ranking for 99 consecutive weeks, but Rybakina will take over on Monday.
Born in Russia, Rybakina represents Kazakhstan. She won her first Grand Slam at Wimbledon in 2022 and now needs only the French Open title to complete a career Grand Slam.
Sabalenka acknowledged Rybakina’s powerful serve and ability to dictate play, particularly on the fast US Open courts.
Rybakina had struggled at the US Open in previous years, never advancing beyond the fourth round before this tournament. She also briefly stopped playing during a quarterfinal match against Iga Swiatek in Cincinnati because of a foot injury but recovered in time for New York.
“I honestly was coming here for the last 10 years, and it was never successful — nothing close to that,” Rybakina said. “It’s just incredible. I’m falling in love with New York more and more.”
Sabalenka had reached the US Open final four straight times and the semifinals six times, but her impressive run at Flushing Meadows ended with Saturday’s defeat.
The Belarusian had won both of her previous meetings with Rybakina this season, at Indian Wells and Miami, and leads their career rivalry 10-8.
Rybakina took the opening set after Sabalenka struggled with her serve and became increasingly frustrated. Sabalenka recovered in the second set, breaking Rybakina late to level the match, but Rybakina quickly regained control in the decider and completed the biggest victory of her career.
